cultural.vision_reason: A hand-printed Tibetan-script Buddhist amulet on daphne-bark paper, showing a chained demonic simian figure — consistent with the Tibetan Buddhist ritual print culture practised by the Monpa of Arunachal Pradesh, a Tibetan-script-using, Vajrayana Buddhist people.

physical.title: print
physical.summary:
Sheet of hand-made paper printed with an amulet design, using a wooden block.  The paper is made from the pulp of the daphne bush.  The designs are of a demonic, simian figure which is chained with strings of text in Tibetan script.  The figure holds a peacock feather in his right hand and a flowering branch in his left; his feet end in claws.  He is in a state of sexual arousal.  The print appears twice on the sheet along with two impressions (the first rather faint) of a strip of Tibetan text which appears at the side of the block.  The sheet of paper is wragged and uneven at the edges.

Prepared for TRB at the Thongmen Gompa, to the east of Tawang.

cultural.vision_reason: A Tibetan-style woodblock prayer-flag print with wind horse, Four Protective Animals, and Tibetan invocatory text, explicitly attributed by the museum to Monpa makers, who share Tibetan Buddhist print traditions. This is a traditional print made and used by the Monpa.

physical.title: print
physical.summary: Woodblock print, on hand-made paper probably from the daphne bush, of the type made for prayer-flags. Ink made of soot from an oil lamp.  In the centre is the 'wind horse' carrying flaming jewels.  At the corners are the canonical Four Protective Animals (clockwise from top left) - garuda (with snakes), dragon, tiger and snow lion.  Between the images are invocatory texts in Tibetan and small auspicious symbols; at the top is the Banner of Victory.

cultural.vision_reason: A block-printed sheet of Tibetan-script mantra text ("Om mani padme hum") made for insertion into a prayer wheel at Gorsam stupa, explicitly attributed to Monpa makers — a traditional religious print used in Monpa Buddhist practice.

physical.title: print
physical.summary: Rectangular sheet of daphne bush hand-made paper, block-printed with 16 lines in Tibetan uncial script, of the mantra 'Om mani padme hum', repeated throughout.  This shape of block-printed sheet is for inclusion inside a prayer-wheel of the type located around the outside of a monument (see 2003. 7-11. 1) and indeed this sheet was given to TRB at the Gorsam stupa when they were re-furbishing the old prayer-wheels.

cultural.vision_reason: A Tibetan Buddhist prayer-flag woodblock print with the "Om mane padme hum" mantra and the Eight Auspicious Symbols, a tradition shared by the Buddhist Monpa people of Arunachal Pradesh who use such prints for prayer flags, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: print
physical.summary: Woodblock print. Rectangular woodblock print on hand-made paper (probably from the daphne bush) and of the type made for prayer-flags. The ink used was prepared from the of soot of an oil lamp. The central panel is filled with the mantra 'Om mane padme hum' repeated continuously.  Around the edges are rectangular panels filled with symbols. Along the top are four of the Eight Auspicious Symbols (l-r,conch-shell, parasol, two fishes and lotus).  Along the bottom are the remaining four (l-r, knot, vase, banner and wheel).  Down each side are eight symbols denoting offerings.
